description: The Vector Search API provides a fully-managed, highly performant, and scalable vector database designed to power next-generation search, recommendation, and generative AI applications. It allows you to store, index, and query your data and its corresponding vector embeddings through a simple, intuitive interface. With Vector Search, you can define custom schemas for your data, insert objects with associated metadata, automatically generate embeddings from your data, and perform fast approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) searches to find semantically similar items at scale.

filter.description: Optional. A JSON filter expression, e.g. `{"genre": {"$eq": "sci-fi"}}`, represented as a `google.protobuf.Struct`. An empty filter (`{}`) matches all data objects. Otherwise, each JSON object in the filter must have exactly one key: either a field name mapped to one operator (`{"price": {"$lt": 100}}`), or a logical operator: `$and` or `$or` with a list of filters, or `$not` with one filter. Field operators and their values: `$eq` and `$ne` take a string, number or bool; `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt` and `$gte` take a number; `$in`, `$nin` and `$all` take a list of strings; `$exists` takes a bool. Several keys in one object (implicit AND) and implicit equality (`{"genre": "sci-fi"}`) are rejected; use `$and` and `$eq` instead. Logical operators can be nested at most 2 levels deep, e.g. `{"$and": [{"$or": [{"a": {"$eq": 1}}, {"b": {"$eq": 2}}]}]}`. Deeper filters are rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

pageToken.description: Optional. The standard list page token. Typically obtained via SearchDataObjectsResponse.next_page_token of the previous DataObjectSearchService.SearchDataObjects call.

nextPageToken.description: Output only. A token to retrieve next page of results. Pass to DataObjectSearchService.SearchDataObjectsRequest.page_token to obtain that page.

results.description: Output only. The list of dataObjects that match the search criteria.

GoogleCloudVectorsearchV1SearchHint.description: Represents a hint to the search index engine.

indexHint.description: Optional. Specifies that the search should use a particular index.

knnHint.description: Optional. If set, the search will use the system's default K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) index engine.

GoogleCloudVectorsearchV1SearchHintIndex.description: Message to specify the index to use for the search.

name.description: Required. The resource name of the index to use for the search. The index must be in the same project, location, and collection. Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/collections/{collection}/indexes/{index}`

targetRecall.description: Optional. The target recall for the search. Must be a double in the range [0, 1]. While the search aims to achieve this level of recall, it is not guaranteed.

GoogleCloudVectorsearchV1SearchHintKnnHi.description: KnnHint will be used if search should be explicitly done on system's default K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) index engine.

dataObject.description: Output only. The matching data object.

distance.description: Output only. Similarity distance or ranker score returned by BatchSearchDataObjects.

filter.description: Optional. A JSON filter expression, e.g. `{"genre": {"$eq": "sci-fi"}}`, represented as a `google.protobuf.Struct`. An empty filter (`{}`) matches all data objects. Otherwise, each JSON object in the filter must have exactly one key: either a field name mapped to one operator (`{"price": {"$lt": 100}}`), or a logical operator: `$and` or `$or` with a list of filters, or `$not` with one filter. Field operators and their values: `$eq` and `$ne` take a string, number or bool; `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt` and `$gte` take a number; `$in`, `$nin` and `$all` take a list of strings; `$exists` takes a bool. Several keys in one object (implicit AND) and implicit equality (`{"genre": "sci-fi"}`) are rejected; use `$and` and `$eq` instead. Logical operators can be nested at most 2 levels deep, e.g. `{"$and": [{"$or": [{"a": {"$eq": 1}}, {"b": {"$eq": 2}}]}]}`. Deeper filters are rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Which filters are accepted depends on how the search is served. If it is served by an approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) index (by default when a ready index exists on `search_field`, or when one is selected via `search_hint.index_hint`), every filtered field must be listed in `Index.filter_fields` at index creation, `$or` and `$all` are accepted only at the top level of the filter, and `$not` and `$exists` are not supported. Not every unsupported filter is rejected: most produce `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, but some are silently ignored, so do not rely on the error. If no ready index exists on `search_field`, or if `search_hint.knn_hint` is set, the search is served by K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) search, which has none of these filter restrictions.

GoogleCloudVectorsearchV1StructuredQuery.description: A structured query for text search. Allows expressing field-targeted text queries combined via boolean operators, with optional per-node boosting.

boost.description: Optional. Optional multiplier applied to this query node's contribution to the final relevance score. Must be non-negative; if unset or 0, defaults to 1.0. Values greater than 1.0 increase its influence on ranking, values between 0.0 and 1.0 decrease it.

combine.description: Optional. A query that combines multiple sub-queries with a boolean operator.

unary.description: Optional. A query that applies a unary operator to a sub-query.

GoogleCloudVectorsearchV1TextQuery.description: A leaf-level text query targeting one or more data fields. When multiple fields are specified, this is equivalent to combining per-field matches with an OR operator (i.e. the query matches if the text is found in any of the listed fields).

fields.description: Required. The data fields to search against.

matchType.description: Optional. The matching strategy to apply for this query. If unset, defaults to `TEXT`.
enumDescriptions: Defaults to `TEXT`.
Treats `text` as individual search terms combined with an implicit AND: every term must appear in the field, in any order and any position. Case-insensitive.
Matches only when the entire field value is exactly equal to `text`.

text.description: Required. The text to search for.

When set, `search_text` and `data_field_names` must be left empty; otherwise the request will be rejected with an `INVALID_ARGUMENT` error. GoogleLongrunningOperation.description: This resource represents a long-running operation that is the result of a network API call.

done.description: If the value is `false`, it means the operation is still in progress. If `true`, the operation is completed, and either `error` or `response` is available.

error.description: The error result of the operation in case of failure or cancellation.

additionalProperties.description: Properties of the object. Contains field @type with type URL.

metadata.description: Service-specific metadata associated with the operation. It typically contains progress information and common metadata such as create time. Some services might not provide such metadata. Any method that returns a long-running operation should document the metadata type, if any.

name.description: The server-assigned name, which is only unique within the same service that originally returns it. If you use the default HTTP mapping, the `name` should be a resource name ending with `operations/{unique_id}`.

additionalProperties.description: Properties of the object. Contains field @type with type URL.

response.description: The normal, successful response of the operation. If the original method returns no data on success, such as `Delete`, the response is `google.protobuf.Empty`. If the original method is standard `Get`/`Create`/`Update`, the response should be the resource. For other methods, the response should have the type `XxxResponse`, where `Xxx` is the original method name. For example, if the original method name is `TakeSnapshot()`, the inferred response type is `TakeSnapshotResponse`.

GoogleRpcStatus.description: The `Status` type defines a logical error model that is suitable for different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details. You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the [API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of google.rpc.Code.

details.description: A list of messages that carry the error details. There is a common set of message types for APIs to use.

additionalProperties.description: Properties of the object. Contains field @type with type URL.

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the google.rpc.Status.details field, or localized by the client.
